reason: The bridge exposes fetch (untrusted web text) plus two servers driving the same shared, non-isolated Chrome profile (logged-in sessions, can navigate/POST anywhere) with no approval step in the bridge. It is a real lethal trifecta only if that browser profile holds private sessions/data; in a throwaway E2B sandbox it may not.
fix: Use --isolated (fresh profile) for chrome-devtools-mcp, keep sensitive logins out of the shared browser, and have the calling agent require approval for navigation/form actions.

evidence.quote: async with httpx.AsyncClient(verify=False, timeout=5) as client:

reason: Unauthenticated GET /health probe of the deployer's own sandbox; no credentials are sent and only the status code is used, so a MITM can at most fake readiness.
fix: Optional: pin the sandbox certificate or use verify=True with the E2B-provided TLS endpoint.

title: /bridge launches any command (or connects to any URL) chosen by the caller

evidence.quote: const { serverPath, method, params, args, env } = req.body;

reason: Any holder of the single ACCESS_TOKEN can POST serverPath='/bin/sh', args=['-c','...'] and get command execution on the gateway host, or give an http(s)/ws URL to make the server connect to internal services (SSRF); nothing restricts it to the configured mcp-servers.json entries. With --tunnel the endpoint is published on the internet.
fix: Remove free-form serverPath/args/env from /bridge and accept only a server id from the operator's config (as /mcp/:serverId does); if URLs are needed, allowlist hosts and block private ranges.

title: X-MCP-ENV-* headers let callers set arbitrary environment variables for spawned servers
reason: A caller can send X-MCP-ENV-NODE-OPTIONS: --require /tmp/x.js, LD_PRELOAD or PATH for an npx/uvx server and run code on the host, or override variables such as N8N_API_URL so a configured server sends its N8N_API_KEY to an attacker host. Even /mcp/:serverId is therefore not limited to operator-defined behaviour.
fix: Accept only an operator-defined allowlist of overridable variable names per server, and never NODE_OPTIONS, LD_*, PATH, *_URL for servers that hold keys.

title: Single static bearer token compared with !==; tunnel publishes the gateway
reason: One shared token gates full host command execution (M001/M002) for every client, the comparison is not constant-time, and --tunnel exposes the port publicly via ngrok; there are no per-client identities, scopes or rate limiting.
fix: Use crypto.timingSafeEqual, per-client tokens with scopes, rate limiting on 401s, and avoid public tunnels for this endpoint.

title: Full tool-call arguments and bridge bodies are logged
reason: maskSensitiveData only masks body.env; tool arguments and args (which can contain API keys, passwords or page content) are written to logs at info level.
fix: Log only method/tool names and sizes, or redact argument values.

title: Unbounded process spawning per request
reason: Every request with new args/env or without a session id starts a new child process; there is no cap on concurrent clients/sessions, so an authenticated caller (or a looping agent) can exhaust the host.
fix: Cap concurrent clients/sessions per token and overall, and rate-limit session creation.

title: Chrome DevTools port bound to 0.0.0.0 without authentication in the 'simple' sandbox template
reason: CDP gives full control of the browser (read pages/cookies, open file:// URLs, navigate) to anyone who can reach port 9222, with no token; whether 9222 is reachable from outside depends on E2B port exposure. startup.sh correctly uses 127.0.0.1.
fix: Bind --remote-debugging-address=127.0.0.1 in every template, as startup.sh does.
